title: Validation of a Deep Learning-Based Detection Tool for Spinal Pathologies of the Lumbar Spine – A Monocentric Retrospective Study
summary: Back pain and changes of the lower spine are very common and are often examined using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). These images are usually assessed by a doctor. Computer programs based on artificial intelligence are now available that can automatically evaluate such images. This study examines how well one such computer program detects changes of the lower spine on existing MRI images, compared to the assessment of experienced doctors. For this purpose, MRI images obtained during routine clinical care are evaluated retrospectively, and the results of the computer program are compared with the doctor's assessment.
conditions: Degenerative and structural changes of the lumbar spine (including disc degeneration, disc bulging, disc herniation, spinal canal stenosis, neuroforaminal stenosis, facet joint arthropathy, endplate changes, spondylolisthesis, vertebral body fractures)

interventions.name: Consecutive lumbar spine MRI examinations (1.5 Tesla) performed between 10 November 2025 and 30 May 2026 at the Department of Diagnostic and Interventional Neuroradiology and Pediatric Neuroradiology, University Hospital Bonn. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Undergoing lumbar spine MRI at the study center during the defined observation period.
Exclusion criteria:
Examinations in which a reliable assessment is not possible (e.g., due to metal artifacts, immediate postoperative findings, tumor findings, inflammatory changes, relevant anatomical variants, or incorrect/insufficient sequences) are excluded, as are patients outside the defined age range.
